title: Genetically Engineered Mouse Model of Brainstem High-Grade Glioma
protocol: Load syringe with 10 μL of plasmid DNA/Jet-PEI solution prepared previously.
Anesthetize first pup prior to plasmid injection by hypothermia.
Wrap the pup in gauze and place it on ice for 2 min.
Place pup on pre-cooled stereotaxic stage and immobilize head using the gauze covered ear bars.
Ensure the pup’s head is secured by the ear bars and parallel to the surface of the stage.
Disinfect injection surface by wiping the pup’s head with 70% ethanol.
Lower the needle to the injection surface.
Adjust stereotaxic coordinates to target the fourth ventricle (3 mm posterior to the lambda suture).
Lower the needle further until a dimple forms on the skin and record the coordinates.
Lower the needle to a depth of 4 mm, then raise it by 1 mm to reach a depth of 3 mm below the skull.
Inject 0.75 μL plasmid solution at a rate of 0.5 μL/min using an automatic injector.
Leave the needle in place for 1 min after injection.
Slowly raise the needle from the skull.
Remove the pup from the stereotaxic frame and place it under a heating lamp.
Monitor the pup’s recovery to ensure normal breathing, mobility, and rosy color return (5–7 min).
Perform gentle lung massage and limb stimulation if needed to aid in recovery.
Limit the time between anesthesia and post-injection warm-up to less than 10 minutes for high survival rates.
Repeat all steps above for remaining injections as necessary.
Return pups to their mother’s cage after injection.
Monitor the mother’s response for 30 min to ensure nurturing behavior resumes.
Monitor plasmid uptake in pups using an IVIS bioluminescence imaging system.
Remove pups from the mother’s cage 24–48 hours after injection.
Anesthetize pups prior to imaging by hypothermia.
Wrap the pups in gauze and place them on ice for 2 minutes.
Place pups individually into wells of a sterile 6-well tissue culture plate.
Use a 1 mL syringe with a 30-gauge hypodermic needle to subcutaneously inject 10 μL of luciferin (30 mg/mL) between pup’s shoulder blades.
Pinch and lift the skin gently prior to injection to prevent penetration of organs.
Wait for 5 min to allow for luciferin to penetrate the brain.
Image pups immediately on IVIS bioluminescence imaging system (IVIS Spectrum settings: automatic exposure, large binning, aperture f = 1).
Place animals in chamber with flowing oxygen and isoflurane (1.5%–2.5% isoflurane, with an oxygen flow of 1.5 L/min [LPM]) to anesthetize.
Remove mouse from chamber and use a 1 mL syringe with a 26-gauge needle to intra-peritoneally inject 100 μL of luciferin (30 mg/mL in PBS or saline).
Set a timer for 5 min.
Place animal back into anesthesia chamber for 3–4 min.
Initiate flow of oxygen and isoflurane to the bioluminescence chamber.
Position animals into imaging slots in the bioluminescence chamber.
Place glass nose cones on the animals in the imaging chamber.
Obtain a series of six images at 2-min intervals when the timer sounds.
Define the area of interest over the head for each animal imaged.
Measure the intensity of luminescence using calibrated units (photons/s/cm2/sr).
Monitor tumor-bearing animals for signs of tumor burden.
Critical: Specific genetic alterations determine the time before neurological deficits appear.
Euthanize tumor bearing mice by transcardial perfusion with Tyrode’s solution supplemented with Heparin (15 Units/L).
Dissect brain from skull and place in sterile Petri dish on damp ice.
Visualize tumor using fluorescent dissecting stereo microscope at appropriate wavelength for fluorescent markers used in SB plasmid mixture.
Isolate fluorescent tumor from surrounding tissue using scalpel.
Transfer isolated tumor into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 300 μL of neural stem cell media.
Dissociate tumor tissue mechanically with plastic pestle.
Add 10 mL of neural stem cell media to the dissociated tumor suspension and filter through 70 μm strainer.
Centrifuge at 2,000 × g for 2 min.
Wash pellet twice with 1 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺, resuspending by pipetting and centrifuging at 2,000 × g for 2 min in each wash.
Incubate tumor suspension with 1 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) Accutase.
Incubate for 2–3 minutes at 37°C.
Add 10 mL of DPBS to the cell suspension and centrifuge cells at 2,000 × g for 2 min.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of NS complete media.
Add NS complete media supplemented with EGF and FGF to a final volume of 10 mL.
Plate cells in a T25 flask and culture at 37°C, 5% CO2 in neural stem cell media.
Centrifuge the neurospheres (500 × g, 2 min) after the first 2 weeks.
Resuspend neurospheres with 10 mL NS media supplemented with growth factors to a final concentration of 20 ng/mL (FGF and EGF).
Replate to a new T25 flask twice a week for the first 2 weeks.
Collect spheres, discarding freely floating single cells or cells adhering to flask.
Passage and replate neurospheres once visible.
Monitor cells for formation of neurospheres.
Change media and replace growth factors as needed until well-formed spheres appear.
Maintain cells in culture.
Passage and expand cells when flasks contain neurospheres and media becomes orange/yellow.
Use cells for implantation and other experiments at a passage below 10.
Take a 70%–90% confluent T-75 flask of neurospheres and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube with a serological pipet.
Centrifuge the tube at 350 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) Accutase.
Incubate for 2–3 min at 37°C.
Gently pipette the solution to ensure proper dissociation of neurospheres.
If necessary, incubate cells longer until fully dissociated.
Filter cells through a 70 μm strainer to remove clumps.
Add 9 mL of PBS and centrifuge at 1,500 rpm (∼350 × g) for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend in 100 μL PBS.
Count cells and dilute to the proper concentration with PBS in a 0.6 mL Eppendorf tube for implantation.
Keep cell suspension on ice (4°C).
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneally injecting ketamine (120 mg/kg) and dexmedetomidine (0.5 mg/kg), dissolved in sodium chloride 0.9% solution.
Shave top of head with animal hair clippers when mouse is sedated and not responsive to pain stimuli.
Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with carprofen (5 mg/kg) dissolved in sodium chloride 0.9% solution.
Place mouse on stereotaxic frame with heat support set to around 37°C.
Open mouth with forceps and place over bite bar, ensuring front teeth go through hole and tongue is pulled to the side.
Press ear bars lightly against sides of head and adjust for stability.
Tighten nose clamp until resistance is felt but not too hard.
Apply iodine to top of head three times, waiting 5 minutes after last application before wiping off.
Make a 0.25 cm incision on skull with scalpel.
Carefully pull back skin from incision using forceps and insert retractors.
Ensure skull is in correct orientation by moving needle along sagittal and coronal sutures.
Maintain parallel alignment of the needle movement with the sagittal and coronal suture lines.
Locate lambda coordinate by pressing lightly near the suture on a slightly dry skin surface.
Move needle 1 mm posterior and 1 mm lateral to lambda coordinate from target site.
Mark location using a tuberculin syringe equipped with a 26-gauge needle by gently scraping periosteum.
Drill through skull at marked location using a #7 or #8 bit connected to a Dremel drill until reaching dura mater.
Use gentle pressure and take breaks during drilling to prevent overheating of the area.
Load Hamilton syringe with cell suspension.
Flick or gently pipette tube containing tumor cells to resuspend cells.
Draw up cell suspension for injection, volume depending on concentration and number of cells.
Eject 1 μL of volume to ensure there is no air in syringe and that cells can be dispensed properly.
Flush injection syringe with PBS prior to loading to ensure it is not clogged and dispenses volume correctly.
Draw more volume than needed when loading cell suspension (e.g., if injecting 1 μL, draw at least 3 μL into syringe).
Lower the syringe to target site until tip barely touches the dura mater.
Lower the syringe 5 mm inferior to the dura mater.
Raise the syringe 0.5 mm and wait 2 min.
Slowly deliver cells at a rate of 1 μL/min.
Wait 5 min after delivery.
Slowly retract the syringe from the brain.
Eject remaining volume in the syringe into a tube containing 10% bleach solution.
Flush needle twice with PBS, then twice with ultrapure sterile water quickly.
Wash injection site three times with sterile PBS.
Loosen nose clamp and ear bars to remove mouse from stereotaxic frame.
Gently remove mouth from bite bar with forceps.
Close incision with 4-0 sutures.
Perform subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine (0.01 mg/kg) followed by intraperitoneal injection of atipamezole (1 mg/kg).
Place the animal in fresh cage with heat support and monitor until full recovery.
